newsitem.title: USA: Donors announce over $3 billion aid to Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Donors announce over $3 billion aid to Lebanon.

text.p: An international donors' conference on Monday pledged more than $3 billion in immediate and long-term aid to Lebanon to help it recover from a 16-year civil war.

A joint statement by Lebanon and the United States said participants announced more than $1 billion in official flows available immediately, and that a number of participants outlined additional multi-year programmes exceeding $2.2 billion.
Delegates from some 30 countries and eight international financial institutions took part in the one-day conference at the State Department.
No official breakdown was immediately available of who was donating the aid, although the United States said earlier its aid to Lebanon would rise to $12 million in 1997 from $2 million this year.
The joint statement said many participants had indicated that Lebanon would also have access to substantial concessional export credit facilities and loan guarantees.

Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri, who attended the conference, had said previously that he would ask the delegates for contributions of up to $5 billion for reconstruction projects in the next five years.
